proof_sketch: Invariance makes F5|P a unitary that maps the E-flat pair to an F-flat pair, so the Bloch normals satisfy n_F = R(F5|P) n_E. Orthogonality forces a rotation by pi/2, so the eigenvalue ratio is +-i, and n_E is perpendicular to the eigen-axis. F5 on C^5 has eigenvalue multiplicities 1:2, -1:1, i:1, -i:1. The ratio-(+-i) pairs are therefore (1 or -1) with (i or -i), with the +-i eigenvectors odd and the +-1 eigenvectors even.
(-1, +-i): the -1 eigenvector is real with |phi(0)|^2=(5-sqrt5)/10, not 2/5.

(1, +-i): the Re-conditions force phi1 to be i times a real vector in the 1-eigenspace span{e1-e2, (1,(sqrt5-1)/(2sqrt2),(sqrt5-1)/(2sqrt2))}. Then |phi1(0)|^2=2/5 forces |phi2(2)|^2/|phi2(1)|^2=(5+-2R)/(5-+2R) with R=sqrt(3sqrt5-5), a value in (0.31,3.2). The actual odd +-i eigenvectors have ratio (lambda-s1)/(lambda+s1)<0.081, or its inverse >12.3, where lambda=sqrt5/2 and s1=sin72. Contradiction, by written interval bounds.
